from.place: Proof, second paragraph of thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general: localization and strict henselization preserve excellence. Through Greco Theorem 5.3(iii)-(iv), this serves Lemma 5.5: its last dimension comparison between C and a maximal localization of its finite normalization.

title: Dimension of a finite normalization of a universally catenary local domain
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian universally catenary local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, and let $C'$ be the integral closure of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], finite as a $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A local ring has one maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero with no zero divisors. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C'$ whose contraction to $C$ is the maximal ideal of $C$, one has $\dim(C'_{\mathfrak m})=\dim C$, where localization is as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.document: literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex; Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Tag 02IJ (lemma-dimension-formula), equality for a universally catenary base, specialized to the finite birational domain extension C ⊂ C′. This is the normalization dimension input cited as [8, Theorem 5.6.10] in Greco Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9).
